title: Coolcicada 6 Days PPL Program review
summary: He reviews the popular Coolcicada 6-day push/pull/legs program from bodybuilding.com, replacing its static 3x5s with evolving rep ranges, reorganising each day with supersets, and cutting redundant lifts. He argues PPL puts a heavy pull day right before leg day, leans toward the lower body, and neglects long-head triceps, calves, traps, rear delts, posterior chain, forearms and neck, so a body part split works better.
claims: Programs from bodybuilding.com that survive community voting are usually not bad
Whether you run PPL-rest-PPL or PPLPPL-rest depends on your ability to return to baseline and whether you prefer to pile up damage and recover in one rest day
A good non-peaking program can be run as long as you keep progressing; one that only works for three months then stalls is bad
Calling a split push/pull/legs and then listing body parts just describes a body part split
3x5 on bench is low horizontal pressing volume; replace it with 3x4-8 to control volume and intensity without losing much tonnage
The overhead press is very hard to progress on; a fixed 3x5 stops working after novice gains, so use 3x4-6 or 3x6-8
His own overhead press uses six sets alternating 3x5 and 3x2-5, e.g. 135x5, 155x3, 145x5, 155x2, to get both high intensity and high volume
A fixed 3x5 is fine on a secondary lift like incline bench where you are not pushing progression; it gives a steady way to add volume
3x10-12 is a good rep scheme for isolation work such as lateral raises, pushdowns, overhead extensions and shrugs

Two compounds that hit different muscles but use the same body, like bench and overhead press, should not be done back to back; two compounds for the same muscle, like back squat then front squat, can be
On his accessory deadlift day he opens with snatch-grip deadlifts and closes with heavy block pulls so both count as strength work
Superset bench press with overhead dumbbell extensions: the triceps long head is not recruited in pressing, and supersetting long-head work with presses has made him stronger

Reorganised push day: bench supersetted with overhead extensions, overhead press supersetted with lateral raises, drop incline bench and pushdowns, optionally add a 3-set giant set of incline bench, pushdowns and shrugs when tonnage is lacking
Moving a lift in and out of the workout is a useful variation hack, but you will not be efficient on a lift you rarely practise
Back and biceps is a low-synergy pairing because the biceps works largely on its own; an arm day gives better synergy
One set of 5 deadlifts is enough for most people when intensity is high; the deadlift drives pulls, rows and lower-body strength but is not the best hypertrophy lift
Pulling from the floor should never be optional; it can be Jefferson, sumo or block pulls, but the pattern must be trained
Deadlifting first warms up hamstrings, glutes and lower back so the following barbell rows are more efficient
3x5 is one of the worst schemes for barbell rows; use 3x6-10 or 3x8-12, because getting 5 reps on every set means it was too easy or your legs took over
3x5 and 5x5 leave too narrow an intensity window, so either volume quality or intensity suffers
Replace lat pulldowns with pull-ups or weighted pull-ups: better for hypertrophy, athleticism and injury prevention
Face pulls should be 3x15-20 rather than 10-12; they should end at muscular failure, never mechanical failure

Following barbell curls straight away with alternate curls raises intensity artificially and lowers tonnage; same-muscle back-to-back work needs a reason, which he only finds for triceps because of their angles

Reorganised pull day: deadlift, barbell rows supersetted with pull-ups, then either superset pulldowns and seated rows for pump or drop both, and finish with face pulls 4x15-20 supersetted with barbell curls 4x10-12
Lower-body days should hold more tonnage than upper-body days because the legs are stronger
With proper technique squats are more taxing than deadlifts; big deadlift-to-squat ratios come from sloppy heavy deadlifts and overly cautious squatting
PPL's core flaw: a heavy pull day directly before leg day with no rest prevents heavy squatting, which is why he promotes body part splits
Bigger muscle groups need more recovery because they move more weight; small muscles recover faster partly because you cannot load them as hard
4x5-6 squats give one rep of breathing room; 4x4-8 is far more useful
Fixed rep schemes help beginners because they give structure and something to blame, but viewers of the channel should use evolving rep ranges
Following squats with leg press is pointless; pick one knee-flexion family (squat, front, SSB, box squat) or leg press and its variations, for specificity
People who think a 500 lb leg press means a 500 lb squat usually squat about 300
Leg extensions are a subpar lift; do more squats instead, and if the lower back limits you add hyperextensions or more hamstring work
Replace hamstring curls with Romanian deadlifts or good mornings for 10-12 reps; the program lacks posterior chain work
Calf work left at the end of a leg session gets skipped; superset calves between heavy sets so you have to do them, like eating spinach before dessert
Reorganised leg day: squats, a lighter squat variation 3x8-12, RDLs or good mornings 4x10-12, with calf raises supersetted for 7-8 total sets
Three sets of long-head triceps work (about 30 reps a week) is not enough for intermediates
PPL is lower-body biased because legs get trained on both pull and leg days, so intermediates end up with good legs and a lacking upper body
Calves need to be trained all the time to grow; almost no program does enough, including his own earlier one, which he revamped
Three sets of 10 shrugs is not enough trap work; nucleus overload inside a body part split would fix it
The program lacks rear delt and posterior chain work; you need more hip hinges, deadlift variations and good mornings
People wrongly treat calisthenics as either only for novices or the only thing advanced lifters need; they should be applied properly, e.g. for lats
Big muscle groups need less frequency than small ones, and horizontal presses tax the shoulders, so chest volume here is enough
Forearms and neck get no direct work in most programs and should
Static rep ranges leave no room to manipulate volume and intensity, so even strength progress on this program will be limited
exercises: hard to progress; needs volume and intensity
long head not recruited in pressing
floor pull must not be optional
pick it or squats, not both
